Surah al-Shu'ara' (The Poets)

[Meccan, except verse 197 and verses 224 onward to the end of the surah, which are Medinan. Its verses number 227. It was revealed after al-Waqi'a.]

﴿Ta-Sin-Mim.﴾ God knows best what He means by this.
﴿Those﴾ i.e., these verses, ﴿are the verses of the Book﴾ the Qur'an, and the idafa (genitive construction) here means "from" (min), ﴿the clear﴾ the one that makes clear the truth from falsehood.

Perhaps (O Muhammad) you are going to destroy yourself ﴿باخِع نَفْسك﴾, killing it with grief ﴿غَمًّا﴾ on account of ﴿مِن أجْل﴾ their not being ﴿ألّا يَكُونُوا﴾ believers ﴿مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, i.e., the people of Makkah. And "perhaps" here is for *ishfaq* (compassionate concern), i.e., he is solicitous for it by easing this grief.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 4:

﴿If We willed, We would send down upon them a sign from the heaven, so that their necks would remain bowed before it﴾ — here "fa-zallat" is in the sense of the present tense: meaning "tazall" (they would remain), i.e. "tadum" (they would continue), ﴿their necks would remain bowed before it﴾, so that they would believe. And since the necks are described with submission (khudu'), which belongs to their owners (arbab, i.e. the people), the attribute was put in the plural form used for rational beings (jam' al-'uqala').

And there does not come to them any reminder, [meaning] the Qur'an, from the Most Merciful, [that is] newly revealed. [Muhdath is a] descriptive adjective (ṣifa kāshifa, an adjective that clarifies its noun).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 6:

﴿So they have denied﴾ it (the Qur'an), ﴿so there will come to them the news﴾ of its consequences.
﴿Have they not looked﴾ at (yanzuru) ﴿the earth, how many of every noble kind We have caused to grow therein?﴾ That is, many, ﴿of every noble pair﴾, a good kind.

Indeed in that is surely a sign (ayah), showing the completeness of His power, the Exalted. "And most of them were not believers" in the knowledge of Allah. Sibawayh said that "kana" here is redundant (za'idah).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 9:

﴿Indeed, your Lord – He is the All-Mighty, the All-Merciful.﴾ Dhu al-'Izza (the Possessor of might), who takes vengeance upon the disbelievers; ﴿the All-Merciful﴾, who shows mercy to the believers.
And mention when your Lord called out to Moses (the night he saw the fire and the tree), saying: "Go to the wrongdoing people" as a messenger.

The people of Pharaoh, with him, wronged themselves by disbelieving in God, and the Children of Israel by enslaving them. ﴿Will they not﴾ (the *hamzah* (the interrogative particle) here is for denunciatory interrogation, *istifham inkari*) ﴿fear God﴾ by obeying Him, so that they would affirm His oneness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 12:

﴿Said﴾ Musa

And my breast will be constricted (by their denial of me), and my tongue will not be freed (to deliver the message) because of the knot that is in it, so send (Gabriel) to Aaron, my brother, to be with me.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 14:

﴿And they have a charge against me﴾ for killing one of them, the Copt, ﴿so I fear that they will kill me﴾ for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 15:

﴿Qāla﴾ (He said), the Exalted said: ﴿Kallā﴾ (No!), they will not kill you. ﴿Fa-dhhabā﴾ (So go), i.e., you and your brother; here the present is given precedence over the absent (taghlīb al-ḥāḍir ʿalā al-ghāʾib). ﴿Bi-āyātinā innā maʿakum mustamiʿūn﴾ (with Our signs; indeed We are with you, listening), to what you say and to what is said to you. The two of them were treated as a group (ujriyā majra al-jamāʿa).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 26, verse 16:

﴿So come to Pharaoh and say: Indeed, we are﴾ each of us ﴿a messenger of the Lord of the worlds﴾ to you.
﴿That﴾, i.e., namely that, ﴿send with us﴾ to al-Sham ﴿the Children of Israel﴾. So come to him and say to him what has been mentioned.

Pharaoh said to Moses: ﴿Did we not bring you up among us as a child﴾, in our houses, ﴿a child﴾ young, close to the time of birth after being weaned, ﴿and you stayed among us for years of your life﴾, thirty years, wearing some of Pharaoh's clothes and riding some of his mounts, and he used to be called his son.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 19:

﴿And you did your deed which you did﴾, which is your killing of the Copt, ﴿and you are of the ungrateful﴾, the deniers of My blessing upon you by raising you and by not enslaving you.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn, commentary on surah 26, verse 20:

﴿He said﴾ Musa, ﴿"I did it then"﴾ i.e., at that time, ﴿"and I was among those who err"﴾ regarding what Allah gave me afterwards of knowledge and prophethood.
﴿So I fled from you when I feared you, then my Lord granted me wisdom﴾ (meaning) knowledge.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 22:

﴿And this is a favour with which you reproach me, that you have enslaved the Children of Israel.﴾ Its original form is "tamunnu bihā ʿalayya" (you reproach me with it). ﴿That you have enslaved the Children of Israel﴾ explains "this" (tilka), i.e., you took them as slaves, and you did not enslave me [as you did them]. "No favour is yours in that, due to your oppression in enslaving them." Some of them (the exegetes) held that at the beginning of the speech there is an implied hamzat al-istifham (interrogative alif), for denial (li-l-inkar).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 23:

﴿Pharaoh said﴾ to Musa, ﴿"And what is the Lord of the worlds?"﴾ — the one you claim to be His messenger. That is: what is He, what is His reality? And since there is no way for created beings to know His essence, exalted is He, and they only know Him through His attributes, Musa (peace be upon him) answered him with some of them:
﴿He said, "Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them"﴾, i.e., the Creator of that, ﴿if you are certain﴾ that He, exalted is He, is their Creator, so believe in Him alone.

Pharaoh said to those around him (ﷺ) — no, correction: the passage has no ﷺ. Here is the translation:

﴿He said﴾ Pharaoh, ﴿to those around him﴾ from the nobles of his people, ﴿"Do you not listen?"﴾ — his answer, which did not correspond to the question.
Musa said: ﴿Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest ones.﴾ And this, although it falls within what came before it, angered Pharaoh, and for that reason
Moses said: ﴿Lord of the East and the West and whatever is between them, if you would but understand﴾ that He is so; so believe in Him alone.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 29:

﴿Pharaoh said﴾ to Moses, ﴿"If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among those imprisoned."﴾ His prison was severe: he would confine the person in a place beneath the earth, alone, where he could see no one and hear no one.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 30:

﴿He said﴾ to him, Moses: ﴿"Even if"﴾ i.e., would you do that even if ﴿I bring you something clear﴾, a manifest proof of my messengership.

Pharaoh said to him: ﴿Then bring it, if you are of the truthful.﴾ In it.

Note: the closing word "فِيهِ" ("in it") is the Jalalayn's brief gloss on the preceding phrase, rendered as it stands.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 32:

﴿So he threw down his staff, and behold, it was a serpent, plainly visible.﴾ A great serpent.

[ونَزَعَ يَده] "And he drew out his hand" — he took it out of his pocket (jayb).
﴿فَإذا هِيَ بَيْضاء﴾ "and behold, it was white" — radiant (dhat shu'a').
﴿لِلنّاظِرِينَ﴾ "to the onlookers" — contrary to what it had been of the brownness (al-udma) it was before.
Pharaoh said to the chiefs around him: "Indeed, this is a skilled sorcerer, learned," i.e., outstanding (fa'iq) in the knowledge of magic.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 36:

﴿They said: Put him off, and his brother, and send into the cities gatherers,﴾ (i.e., delay their matter), ﴿who will bring you every skilful sorcerer﴾ (i.e., assemblers).
﴿They will bring you every skilled, knowledgeable sorcerer﴾, who surpasses Musa in the knowledge of magic.

Translation:

﴿So the magicians were assembled for the appointed time of a known day﴾ and it was the time of mid-morning (ḍuḥā) on the day of the festival (yawm al-zīna).
﴿And it was said to the people, "Will you gather?"﴾ The interrogative (istifham) is for urging (al-hath) them to assemble.
The expression of hope (al-tarajji) is, on the assumption that they (the magicians) would prevail, so that they would continue upon their religion and not follow Musa.

﴿Then when the magicians came, they said to Pharaoh: "Will we truly have a reward﴾, pronouncing the two hamzas (the glottal stops) distinctly (tahqiq), softening the second (tashil), and inserting an alif between them, in both ways of reading.

Translation of the passage:

﴿He said, "Yes, and indeed you will then be among those brought near."﴾ That is, at that time.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 43:

﴿Musa said to them﴾ after they had said to him: ﴿Either you throw, or we will be the ones who throw﴾. ﴿Throw what you are going to throw﴾. The imperative here is for permission, to let them throw first, as a means of bringing the truth to light.

﴿Then Moses cast down his staff, and behold, it swallowed﴾ with one of the two *tā'*s removed from the original form, so that it reads تَلْقَف (*talqaf*), meaning it swallows (تَبْتَلِع). ﴿what they falsify﴾: they reverse it (يَقْلِبُونَهُ) through their deception (بِتَمْوِيهِهِمْ), so they imagined their ropes and their staffs to be snakes that move (حَيّات تَسْعى).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 48:

﴿The Lord of Moses and Aaron﴾ (because of their knowledge that what they had witnessed of the staff could not be accomplished by sorcery).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 49:

﴿He said: "Have you believed in Him"﴾ Pharaoh (said), with both hamzas pronounced as hamzas, and the second changed to an alif (in reading "āmantum" as it stands), ﴿before I give you permission﴾ to ﴿Him﴾, to Musa, ﴿before I give you permission. Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic﴾, so he taught you some of it and overcame you with something else. ﴿But you will come to know﴾ what will befall you from me, ﴿I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on alternate sides﴾, meaning the right hand of each one and the left foot.
﴿They said, "No harm [will come to us]"﴾: there will be no harm upon us in that, ﴿"Indeed, we are to our Lord"﴾ after our death, in whatever manner it occurs, ﴿"returning"﴾ to Him in the Hereafter.
﴿Innā naṭma‘** (We hope)** ﴾ — "narjū" (we hope) — ﴿that our Lord will forgive us our sins, that⦆ — i.e., because — ﴿we were the first of the believers⦆ — in our time.

And We revealed to Musa ﴿And We revealed to Musa﴾ after years he had spent among them, calling them with the signs of Allah to the truth, but they only increased in defiance. ﴿That, travel by night with My servants﴾, the Children of Israel. In one qira'a (a recognised canonical reading) the nun is vowelled with a kasra and the hamza of أسِرْ (asir) is pronounced with wasl, from سَرى (sara), a dialect (lugha) form of أسْرى (asra). That is: travel with them by night to the sea. ﴿Indeed, you will be pursued﴾: Pharaoh and his soldiers will follow you, so they will plunge into the sea after you, and I will save you and drown them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 53:

﴿Then Pharaoh sent [heralds]﴾ when he was informed of their departure, ﴿into the cities﴾. It is said that he had a thousand cities and twelve thousand villages. ﴿Gatherers﴾, i.e., gathering the army, saying:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 54:

﴿Indeed, these are a small band﴾ (shirdhima), a company, ﴿few in number﴾ (qalilun). It is said that they were six hundred thousand and seventy thousand, and the vanguard of his army was seven hundred thousand. So he belittled them in comparison with the greatness of his army.
﴿And indeed, they are enraging us﴾, doing what angers us.
And indeed we are all wary (ḥādhirūn) [meaning:] prepared (mustaʿiddūn). And in another reading, ḥādhirūn [is read as] vigilant (mutayaqqiẓūn).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 26, verse 59:
